themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints spiked to 29 reports last week—a 209% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 9.4 weekly complaints—marking the largest single-week surge in residential noise in CD 210 over the past two months.
evidence: 29 noise complaints last week vs. 9.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (209% spike, z-score: 4.39)
Noise - Residential is 4th highest complaint category overall (754 complaints over 90 days), but weekly volume just tripled
No corresponding Reddit discussions or local news coverage yet—ground-level story still unbroken
reporting_angles: Door-knock reporting: interview affected residents in high-complaint blocks to identify source (construction, new venue, changed enforcement?)
NYPD data: pull noise violation summonses issued in CD 210 last week to see if enforcement changed or if complaints reflect new actual problem

themes_detail.label: Appliance Failures & Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints jumped to 13 reports last week—a 352% spike above the 8-week baseline of 2.9 per week—suggesting a possible pattern of building-wide appliance failures, utility issues, or unreported maintenance backlog.
evidence: 13 appliance complaints last week vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (352% increase, z-score: 5.52)
Heat/Hot Water remains top concern in district (910 complaints over 90 days); appliance surge may be related infrastructure symptom
Timing aligns with winter season when heating systems, boilers, and water appliances are under peak stress
reporting_angles: Interview HPD or building managers: are there specific buildings or addresses with repeated failures? Suggest systemic maintenance issue.
Check DOB permits: have complaint buildings filed for major alterations or boiler replacements? Look for patterns.

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints exploded to 4 reports two weeks ago—a 3100% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week—indicating possible removal of trash receptacles, overflow crisis, or sanitation service gap affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 4 litter basket complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72—highest z-score in dataset)
Unsanitary Condition complaints also elevated (220 total over 90 days); litter basket removal could cascade into broader sanitation complaints
Community board budget requests include ongoing DEP capital requests, suggesting chronic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: DSNY follow-up: confirm whether trash receptacles were removed, relocated, or are in overflow state in affected blocks
Visual inspection: photograph specific blocks where complaints clustered to show sanitation conditions

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Action Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged to 4 reports last week—a 1500% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week—potentially signaling either new illegal vending activity or a sudden enforcement crackdown in the district.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Spike is very recent (last week only); no sustained trend yet, suggesting either sudden enforcement action or new violation wave
No accompanying Reddit or news coverage; complaint source and nature (street vendors, food carts, informal markets?) unclear from data alone
reporting_angles: DCA/NYPD records: obtain vendor violation summonses and enforcement actions issued in CD 210 last week to confirm new crackdown or new activity
Street-level reporting: identify which blocks or commercial corridors are seeing enforcement; interview vendors and local merchants about changes

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Safety Concerns Rising
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints tripled to 3 reports 3 weeks ago (700% spike from 0.4 baseline), paired with a 433% spike in Safety complaints (4 reports 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 baseline), signaling emerging homelessness and safety issues in the district over the past month.
evidence: Encampment complaints: 3 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Safety complaints: 4 reports 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 3.92)
Two concurrent spikes suggest linked phenomenon—encampments driving safety complaints, or safety concerns attracting both types of complaints
reporting_angles: Walk three major parks/green spaces in CD 210 (identify from 321 DOB permits filed); document encampment locations, size, duration, resident needs
Interview DHS/Homeless Services: are shelters full? Is outreach capacity adequate for district? Cross-reference with 311 complaint locations.
